title: What is the work-block command called?
description:
## Question

The glossary settles on 'work block' for a logged stretch of one contributor's work and says to avoid 'session' for it, because 'Claude session' means one conversation with Claude Code. The command is currently 'goodall session start|end|status' and a constant is SESSION_GATE_CLOSED. Should the command be renamed (for example 'goodall block ...' or 'goodall work ...'), or should 'session' stay as the command word with the glossary recording that? Whatever is chosen is applied to the CLI help, constants, tests, AGENTS.md and open issues.

title: Does goodall adopt a terminal library or print plainly?
description:
## Question

All terminal input and output goes through one UI module (AGENTS.md invariant 9). Should that module be built on a third-party terminal library, or on the standard library alone with a library adopted later only if the onboarding wizard proves to need one? Decide using the provenance findings, the readability bar for researchers, and the rule that hook code can never import the library.

title: Which terminal libraries could goodall adopt, and what is their provenance?
description:
## Question

Goodall's wizard and diagnostic need prompts, tables and readable failure output. Establish, from primary sources and dated today, the candidates and their facts for the dependency rule in docs/DEPENDENCIES.md: at least rich (the predecessor's choice, re-verify), questionary and prompt_toolkit (rejected by the predecessor, re-verify), and any other credible option; for each the maintainer or organisation, repository and activity, advisory history, licence, and direct and transitive dependency count. Also establish what the standard library alone can do (input(), getpass, textwrap, shutil.get_terminal_size, ANSI codes) and its limits on macOS terminals.
close_reason: Provenance facts gathered for five terminal libraries and the standard library; findings on branch research/terminal-library-provenance.

comments.author: Luke Thomas
comments.text:
Resolved by a research subagent (Claude Opus 5.5) on 2026-11-16. Full findings with source links: docs/research/terminal-library-provenance.md on branch research/terminal-library-provenance (commit 6cd7879; never merged, no pull request).

Gist, facts only:
- rich 15.0.0 (MIT): Textualize, the company behind it, closed in 2025; Will McGugan now maintains it essentially alone. 3 packages installed. No advisories on rich; one low-severity Pygments issue fixed in 7 days. Tables and typed prompts, no arrow-key selection.
- questionary 2.1.1 (MIT, marked Beta): one maintainer, no release in 15 months. 2 packages installed. Every prompt type, no tables.
- prompt_toolkit 3.0.53 (BSD-3): effectively one maintainer. 1 package installed. No advisories.
- click 8.5.1 (BSD-3): Pallets volunteer team, six public members, the most active candidate. Zero dependencies, no advisories. Prompt, confirm, hidden input, single-key read and an editor hand-off for multi-line text; no list selector, no tables.
- InquirerPy 0.3.4: one maintainer, no commits since 2022.
- Standard library: input(), getpass, shutil.get_terminal_size and tty/termios cover text, hidden input and single-key reads. textwrap counts characters not display columns and does not handle ANSI codes. No tables, no list selector, no colour API. On macOS readline may be libedit.
- Could not verify: dependency counts from a real resolve; PyPI owner lists for most packages; who else can release rich or prompt_toolkit; import-time figures other than rich's published ~18 ms.

title: How are secret references represented now that an equivalent secrets manager is allowed?
description:
## Question

ADR 0006 requires every credential to be a reference into 1Password or an equivalent secrets manager, resolved at the moment of use, with 1Password the only one supported today. The predecessor used a .env file of op:// references resolved by 'op run'. How should goodall represent a secret reference so that 1Password works now and another manager can be added without changing the format: keep .env with manager-specific reference strings, or name the manager and the reference separately? What must goodall be able to check about a reference without ever resolving it?

title: What does the runner gateway's interface look like?
description:
## Question

All subprocess and network calls go through one runner module with a fake for tests (AGENTS.md invariant 9). Sketch the interface to react to: what a caller passes and gets back for a command, whether HTTP requests belong in the same gateway or a separate one, how timeouts are expressed, how a test scripts the fake's answers and asserts on what was called, and whether real git (which tests are allowed to use) goes through the gateway too. The predecessor had CommandRunner with run() and http_get(), a SubprocessRunner and a FakeRunner; say what to keep and what to change.

title: What is eval-wide and what is local to one machine?
description:
## Question

The record repo is shared by every contributor to an eval, so what it holds must be true for all of them. Some settings are true only for one machine or one person: which contributor am I, where is my log directory, where is my copy of the record repo. Which settings belong in the eval config in the record repo, which belong in a machine-local file, and can a secret reference ever appear in either?

comments.author: Luke Thomas
comments.text:
Resolved by grilling with the owner on 2026-11-16. Recorded as ADR 0009 (docs/adr/0009-eval-config-is-shared-and-local-settings-are-not.md); GLOSSARY.md updated (contributor narrowed to a person, roster added, eval config, local settings and declared scope redefined).

Decisions, each agreed by the owner:
1. A contributor is always a person. Agents are not contributors; records identify them by model and tool, and actor labels distinguish their entries.
2. The eval config holds a roster (id and display name per contributor); local settings hold one of those ids, saying which contributor this macOS user account is.
3. The eval config holds exactly: the eval's name and description, the roster, workstreams, declared scope, intervention categories and a schema version. The construct stays its own file in the record repo.
4. The declared scope names repositories by identity (and paths inside them), never by a local filesystem path.
5. Secret references appear only in local settings, never in the eval config. Accepted cost: each contributor sets up their own references at onboarding.
6. The roster holds no email addresses; commit authorship in the record repo comes from git's own settings.
7. The record repo's remote lives only in git. Onboarding asks for the URL once; goodall stores it nowhere else.
8. Local settings never override the eval config. The two files hold different keys.
9. Machine facts (hostname, macOS version, goodall version, Claude Code version) are recorded on each work block automatically and configured in neither file.

So local settings hold: record repo location, log directory location, contributor id, and secret references.

title: How does goodall find an eval's config and log directory from any folder?
description:
## Question

A goodall command or a Claude Code hook can run from any working directory, in any repository the eval touches. Something must tell it where the record repo (which holds the eval config) and the log directory are. One eval account holds one eval. What is that something: a file at a fixed place in the account's home, an environment variable, a search upward from the working directory, or a combination, and what happens when it is missing or points somewhere that does not exist (for example an unmounted log volume)?
close_reason: One eval per macOS user account, found through local settings at a fixed place in the account's home; see ADR 0008.

comments.author: Luke Thomas
comments.text:
Resolved by grilling with the owner on 2026-11-16. Recorded as ADR 0008 (docs/adr/0008-one-eval-per-macos-user-account-found-through-local-settings.md); terms 'local settings' and 'macOS user account' added to GLOSSARY.md.

Decisions, each agreed by the owner:
1. One macOS user account holds exactly one eval. Two evals in one macOS user account is unsupported; two on one Mac is fine when each has its own macOS user account.
2. Discovery is one file at a fixed place in the account's home, under ~/.config/goodall/. Not an environment variable (not reliably present) and not an upward search (work happens in repos that are not the record repo).
3. One environment variable (working name GOODALL_CONFIG_DIR) may override that location and is honoured everywhere, including hooks, so tests and goodall's own development never touch a real home folder. It is the only override.
4. That file holds the local settings: where this account's record repo is, where its log directory is, and which contributor this account is. Everything else comes from the eval config in the record repo. The chain is local settings -> record repo -> eval config.
5. When local settings are missing or unreadable, the prompt gate refuses the prompt with the fix; ordinary commands fail with the same message and exit code 1.
6. When the log directory cannot be reached, that counts as not recording: no work block is reported active and the gate refuses.
7. The file's contents are called 'local settings' (avoid local config, machine config, pointer file).
8. Write 'macOS user account' in full, shortening to 'account' only where the same paragraph has already used the full term; avoid 'profile'.

Left for the spec: the file's exact name, and the final name of the override variable.

title: Map: a spec for goodall's foundations
description:
## Destination

A spec for goodall's foundations (the runner gateway, the UI gateway and the eval config model), ready to hand to `/to-tickets`. The spec supersedes the existing Foundations issues "Build runner and UI gateways with a fake runner" (goodall-yjt.3) and "Define project config model" (goodall-yjt.4), and settles "Align command and constant names with the glossary's 'work block' and 'prompt gate'" (goodall-yjt.7). Those three are blocked on this map until it closes.

## Notes

- Domain: goodall, a tool that records what a person and their AI agents each did during an open-world eval. Read `GLOSSARY.md` and the ADRs in `docs/adr/` first.
- Use the glossary's terms, and update `GLOSSARY.md` the moment a term settles (domain-modeling skill).
- Write an ADR only when a decision is hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the result of a real trade-off.
- Consult the codebase-design skill for the gateway tickets; they are interface design.
- Any new dependency needs the owner's approval and a row in `docs/DEPENDENCIES.md`.
- Code run by hooks imports only the standard library (ADR 0005).
- Settled while charting, 2026-11-16, by the owner: the eval config is written in TOML. Hooks must read at least the log directory location, so the format has to be one the standard library parses; that rules out YAML, and TOML was chosen over JSON.
- Research subagents may push `research/*` branches. They are never merged and get no pull request.
- This map plans. It ends when the spec can be written with nothing left to decide.

## Decisions so far

<!-- one line per closed ticket: [title](id): gist -->

- [Which terminal libraries could goodall adopt, and what is their provenance?](goodall-xes.5): every candidate with tables or list prompts has one effective maintainer (rich lost its company in 2025); click has a team and no dependencies but no tables or list selector; the standard library covers text, hidden input and single keys only. Findings on branch research/terminal-library-provenance.

- [How does goodall find an eval's config and log directory from any folder?](goodall-xes.1): one eval per macOS user account, found through local settings at a fixed place in the account's home (one override variable); a missing file or unreachable log directory closes the prompt gate. ADR 0008.

## Not yet specified

- The eval config's and the local settings' actual fields and file names, and the final name of the override variable. Waits on what is eval-wide versus local to a machine, and how secret references are represented.
- How goodall writes TOML, given the standard library only reads it (a template at onboarding, or a small writer).
- How a failure carries its "what to do next" text, and how human-readable output and `--json` output relate. Waits on the terminal library decision.
- Where tests take hold of the program to swap in the fake runner. Waits on the runner gateway's interface.

## Out of scope

- The open-source README (goodall-yjt.5): writing, and it depends on later epics.
- The record repo's git operations (write, commit, push): they belong to the Record repo epic (goodall-g1k).

title: Claude hooks that stop agents committing to a branch whose PR is merged
description: Luke's request 2026-11-16: in other projects agents added commits to branches just after he merged their PRs. Add project hooks so an agent learns the branch's merge status at session start and periodically, and is blocked from git commit and git push on a branch whose pull request is already merged, with instructions to start a new branch from the default branch.
acceptance_criteria: Outside-in tests drive the hook script with real hook input, a real git repo and a fake gh; a commit on a merged branch is refused with the fix; unmerged branches, main, and non-git commands pass; a gh failure fails open with a note.
close_reason: Hook script, tests, settings registration and AGENTS.md rule committed on branch claude/branch-merge-status-hooks (3 commits). Verified against real GitHub by pipe-test; not yet observed firing inside a live session (settings load at session start). Not pushed.

title: goodall export scout
description: Build an Inspect Scout transcript database: Claude sessions through Scout's own claude_code importer, plus goodall's work blocks, journal entries and interventions mapped to the matching Inspect event types or transcript metadata, with actor labels attached. inspect-ai and inspect-scout are an optional extra imported only here; needs dependency approval first.
acceptance_criteria: Scout can open the exported database and filter by work block, actor label and intervention category; capture works with the extra uninstalled.

title: Parse human actions from Claude Code transcripts
description: From raw transcripts, identify what the human actually did: typed prompts (as distinct from tool results and harness-injected text), interruptions, and permission approvals and denials. Written in the style of the Inspect importer so it can be offered upstream.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture transcripts covering each action type parse correctly; unknown entry types are reported, never silently dropped.

title: Actor labelling rules, version 1
description: Compute a label of human, ai or harness for every transcript entry and every goodall record by documented rules that carry a version. Output is derived data; raw files are untouched. Luke expects to iterate on these rules during the sprint, so the rules must be easy to read, change and re-run.
acceptance_criteria: Rules documented alongside the code; re-running with a new rule version regenerates labels; a report lists entries no rule matched.

title: Open an upstream issue on human actions in the Claude Code importer
description: Draft for Luke to file with the Inspect maintainers: the Claude Code importer (logic in inspect_swe) creates no event for user prompts, interrupts or permission decisions, and a rejected tool call appears only as an unknown error. Propose surfacing them as InputEvent, InterruptEvent and ApprovalEvent. Check both repos' contributing rules and existing issues first (inspect_ai #6520, inspect_scout #629).
design:
TARGET REPO: meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swe (mapping code lives in src/inspect_swe/_claude_code/_events/; inspect_scout wraps it; fixture tests live in inspect_scout, so a PR likely touches both).

DRAFT ISSUE (for Luke to review, edit and file himself):

Title: Claude Code transcript import: record user interrupts and tool-use rejections as events

## Feature request

**Problem.** `_claude_code/_events` (used by inspect_scout's `claude_code()` source) records nothing for the human's actions in a session other than prompt text:

- Typed prompts become `ChatMessageUser` with no `source` (extraction.py L37-80, `extract_user_message`) and appear only inside a later `ModelEvent`'s input. `isMeta`/`userType` are not read, so typed prompts and injected text look the same.
- Interrupt markers ("[Request interrupted by user]") are kept as ordinary user text. No `InterruptEvent` is emitted.
- A rejected tool call becomes `ToolCallError(type="unknown")`, the same as any other tool failure (events.py L243-256). Feedback the user gave with the denial stays inside the error string.

/clear and compaction are already handled (`split_on_clear`, `CompactionEvent`).

**Why.** Analysing human-in-the-loop sessions needs to find where the person stepped in. Today that means pattern-matching message text against strings Claude Code may change.

**Proposal** (existing types only):
1. Rejection -> `ApprovalEvent(call=<ToolCall>, approver="human", decision="reject", explanation=<feedback or None>)` before the `ToolEvent`, with `ToolEvent.error.type="approval"`.
2. Interrupt -> `InterruptEvent(source="user_cancel", interrupted="tool_call" | "generate", interrupted_tool_call_id=...)`.
3. Typed prompts -> `ChatMessageUser(source=...)` for non-meta user entries.

Detection strings in one function, with fixture tests; unknown shapes fall back to current behaviour.

**Questions.**
- Is `ApprovalEvent` right for a rejection with no approval policy? Approvals aren't in the transcript, so only rejections would appear.
- Should `approver` be "human", with the person in `metadata["decided_by"]` as in inspect_ai#6520?
- Should typed prompts use `source="input"` or `"operator"`, or should they get an event of their own?
- Which repo should own this: here, or in inspect_scout, where the fixtures live?

I can implement this with fixture transcripts (interrupt, deny, deny with feedback) if accepted.

*Drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code); I've reviewed it and checked the references against main.*
acceptance_criteria: Luke has reviewed and filed the issue; its URL is saved with bd remember.
notes: Source verified 2026-11-16 at inspect_swe c50ce3c, inspect_scout bf32fa3, inspect_ai 8c2e11f. Related: inspect_swe#66 (operator intervention through the bridge, the live counterpart), inspect_ai#6520 (decided_by metadata convention), inspect_scout#629, inspect_ai PRs #6487 and #6296 (merged, live path). Rules: inspect_swe has no issue-first text but PR titles must be Conventional Commits and an agent-co-authored PR needs an '### Agent review' section; inspect_scout/inspect_ai need an 'accepted' issue before code. LOCAL EVIDENCE from 277 transcripts on this machine (Claude Code 2.1.274 era): '[Request interrupted by user]' 111 and '[Request interrupted by user for tool use]' 24, almost all as plain text blocks with no toolUseResult; rejections appear as tool_result blocks with is_error true and a STRING toolUseResult ('User rejected tool use' x30, 'Error: The user doesn't want to proceed with this tool use.' x8); denial feedback follows 'the user said:'. userType was 'external' on all 57,221 user entries, so userType does NOT separate typed prompts from injected text; isMeta was true on 1,007. Draft item 3 was adjusted accordingly. Not verified: whether approvals are recorded at all; marker stability across Claude Code versions. Luke must review the draft and file it; nothing has been posted.

title: Attribution and analysis: labels, human actions, Scout export
description: Turning raw records into an analysable, attributed dataset, with the parsing shaped for contribution to Inspect. Decisions: bd memories DECISION.

title: goodall dry-run: end-to-end capture check
description: Scripted verification that a real work block produces a transcript copy, a work-block record in the record repo, a journal entry, and Collector output when enabled, then reports each as pass or fail with a fix. Replaces the old toy prototype command (CRUX recommendation 5).
acceptance_criteria: Running it on a correctly set-up account passes every line; breaking any one piece fails exactly that line.

title: goodall onboard wizard
description: Asks for project, contributor, record repo location and remote, scope, workstreams and billing; shows every planned change and writes only on confirmation; safe to re-run with previous answers as defaults; non-interactive answers file; installs the Claude Code hooks into the account's user settings; offers to write the construct file into the record repo.
acceptance_criteria: Re-running and accepting defaults reports every file unchanged; an answers file containing a raw secret is rejected; hooks appear in user settings without disturbing existing ones.

title: goodall doctor
description: Read-only checks with a fix for every failure; a failed prerequisite marks dependents skipped rather than cascading; --json and --offline. Checks: tools present, account is standard, 1Password signed in when any secret is referenced, .env hygiene, GitHub token validity and scope only when the record remote is GitHub, record repo state (warn on no remote or public GitHub remote), hooks installed, Collector version.
acceptance_criteria: Each check has a passing and failing test with remediation text; a full run with the network down finishes within 30 seconds.

title: Setup and verification: onboard, doctor, dry run, teardown
description: The wizard that sets an eval account up, the read-only diagnostic, the end-to-end dry run, and the teardown wizard promised in the sprint application. Decisions: bd memories DECISION.

title: Telemetry receiver: capture Claude Code's OpenTelemetry export
description: Goodall's own standard-library receiver for Claude Code's OTLP http/json export (decision 2026-11-16; the official Collector is optional, not a dependency). Listens on 127.0.0.1 only, accepts POSTs to /v1/logs, /v1/metrics and /v1/traces, and appends each request body verbatim as one line to a per-signal JSON Lines file under the log directory, flushed per write. Started with a work block and stopped at its end; the work-block record states whether telemetry was captured. Because Claude Code silently drops telemetry when nothing is listening, the hook path checks the receiver is up and doctor reports it. Onboarding sets the Claude Code telemetry environment (enable flag, exporters, http/json protocol, endpoint, traces beta flag). Open questions to settle when building: whether prompt, response and tool-detail content flags are on by default (transcripts already hold content; telemetry carries email and account ids on every record either way); how the receiver process is supervised across sleep and crashes. Evidence and field lists: bd memories SPIKE goodall-fs9.2.
acceptance_criteria: Start from a failing outside-in test: a fake Claude Code POST to the receiver results in one verbatim line in the right file. A real work block yields logs, metrics and traces files whose session.id matches the transcript filename; killing the receiver mid-session loses no already-acknowledged line; a work block with the receiver down still captures transcripts and records telemetry as missing; capture code imports only the standard library.

title: goodall hook: prompt gate and heartbeat
description: Entry point Claude Code hooks call. UserPromptSubmit refuses the prompt with the fix ('goodall session start') when no work block is active; every event records a heartbeat and links the Claude session id to the work block. Imports standard library only.
acceptance_criteria: A test asserts the hook module imports nothing third-party; gate refusal and pass-through both tested from recorded hook input; measured start-up time noted.
notes: Design inputs from spike fs9.1: gate via UserPromptSubmit exit 2 + stderr reason or JSON {decision:block}; claude -p exits 0 on refusal, so callers cannot use the exit code; refused prompt text still lands in the transcript (queue-operation and system entries); ~30ms overhead for a stdlib python hook; heartbeat on PostToolUse.

title: Incremental transcript sync
description: Copy Claude Code transcripts verbatim into the log directory in Claude Code's own layout (including subagent files) after each response via an async Stop hook, with SessionEnd as a top-up and a sweep on the next session start or any goodall command. Never overwrite a copy when the source has shrunk; keep both.
acceptance_criteria: Killing a session mid-turn loses nothing after the next sweep; Scout's claude_code importer reads the copied directory unchanged; shrink case tested.
notes: Design inputs from spike fs9.1: trigger incremental copy on PostToolUse (per tool call) as well as Stop (once per run) and SessionEnd; a copy at PostToolUse is one step behind by nature; async hooks are SIGTERMed at process exit so the copy must be fast and atomic (write temp then rename); SIGKILL fires no hooks, so the sweep on next start is the only guarantee; copy the <session_id>/subagents/ folder including .meta.json and .prefix.json.

title: Work blocks: goodall session start, end, status
description: A work block records contributor, workstream, billing mode, start and end. State is a marker file inside the log directory created atomically; records are append-only; a leftover marker is recovered, never deleted. End states: clean, abnormal, inferred (closed at last heartbeat). status --json is stable for agents.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover racing starts, crash recovery, unreachable log directory, and inferred end from heartbeats; status exits 0 when active and 1 when not.

title: Spike: OpenTelemetry Collector with Claude Code
description: Run the official Collector (>= v0.165.0, bound to localhost) with the file exporter against a real Claude Code session. Record which export protocols Claude Code offers, what events and metrics arrive with the OTEL_LOG_* content flags on and off, what cost_usd reports on subscription vs API-key sessions, and whether file exporter output follows the OTLP file spec. Note install route for a standard account.
acceptance_criteria: Go/no-go recommendation saved with bd remember, with a sample output file layout and any upstream issues worth filing.
notes: Both halves done; findings in three bd memories (SPIKE goodall-fs9.2 ...). Recommendation: own stdlib receiver, Collector optional. Awaiting Luke's decision before closing and before rewriting goodall-fs9.7.
close_reason: Spike complete. Outcome: goodall uses its own stdlib OTLP receiver; the Collector is optional (decision saved 2026-11-16). Findings in three bd memories titled SPIKE goodall-fs9.2.

title: Capture: hooks, work blocks, transcripts, collector
description: Recording AI work as it happens without depending on a clean session end. Decisions: bd memories DECISION.

title: Spike: Claude Code hook and transcript behaviour
description: Establish by experiment what the docs leave open: does SessionEnd fire on terminal close, kill, sleep; does compaction rewrite or append the transcript file; do resumed sessions keep their id; exact stdin fields per hook event; where subagent transcripts land; cost of a synchronous UserPromptSubmit hook in Python.
acceptance_criteria: Findings saved with bd remember, each marked observed (with Claude Code version) or still unknown.
notes: Partial: gate, stdin fields for 3 events, resume, overhead and dir naming observed (see bd memories SPIKE). Blocked on nested claude -p auth (OAuth session expired) for everything needing a model reply.
close_reason: Headless behaviour established and saved to bd memories (two SPIKE entries). Human-only questions split into goodall-fs9.8, fs9.9, fs9.10.

title: Add goodall journal and goodall intervene
description: Commands that create a journal or intervention entry from an argument or stdin (no editor required, so agents can call them), stamped with contributor, work block and category, then written through the record repo layer.
acceptance_criteria: Each command produces one valid file and one commit; --json returns the entry id; an intervention without a valid category fails with the list of valid ones.

title: Operate the record repo: write, commit, push
description: Adopt an existing local or cloned repo at record.path; write one file per entry; commit locally first; push when record.remote is set; a failed push never blocks the write and is retried on the next one. Goodall never creates the remote or changes its visibility.
acceptance_criteria: Tests with real git cover: no remote, reachable remote, unreachable remote then recovery, two contributors writing without conflict.

title: Specify record schemas aligned to Inspect events
description: Published schemas for work-block records (JSON) and journal and intervention entries (Markdown with a metadata header). Intervention fields reuse Inspect's ApprovalEvent decision values, InterruptEvent source/interrupted values and InputEvent outcomes; every record carries contributor id, timestamps (UTC), work-block id and schema version.
acceptance_criteria: Schema documents committed; an example of each record type validates; mapping table to Inspect event types written.

title: Record repo: goodall-run store for an eval's own records
description: The separate git repo goodall operates for each eval: config, construct, journal, interventions, work-block records. One file per entry, contributor id on every record. Decisions: bd memories DECISION.

title: Define project config model
description: Schema, validation, read and write for an eval's project.yml: project, contributors (id, name, kind), record.path, record.remote (optional), declared scope (repos and paths), workstreams, billing modes, intervention categories (default CRUX's four). Plus the .env reader/linter that accepts only op:// references for credential-named variables.
acceptance_criteria: Round-trip tests pass; a raw secret value is rejected with a fix; schema_version present.

title: Build runner and UI gateways with a fake runner
description: One module through which every subprocess and network call passes (explicit timeouts, fake implementation for tests) and one module for all terminal input/output. AGENTS.md invariant 9.
acceptance_criteria: No other module imports subprocess, urllib or the terminal library; tests demonstrate the fake runner.

title: Create package skeleton and the goodall command
description: pyproject.toml for distribution 'goodall' (Python >=3.12, uv, src layout), one console script 'goodall' using argparse subcommands, pytest wired up. Subcommands may be stubs that exit 2 with a 'not built yet' message.
acceptance_criteria: uv sync works; 'uv run goodall --help' lists the planned subcommands; 'uv run pytest' passes; exit codes 0/1/2/3 documented in one place.
notes: Skeleton built and verified with python3.12 + stdlib test loop (9 tests pass). NOT yet verified: pytest discovery, hatchling build, the installed console script; these wait on dependency approval (goodall-yjt.2). Stubs exit 1 (error), not 2 as the original acceptance text said. Uncommitted.
close_reason: Skeleton built; verified after tooling approval: uv sync installs it, 'uv run goodall' works, 9 pytest tests pass, ruff and mypy --strict clean. Uncommitted on branch claude/bluedot-eval-harness-rebuild-ec29e4.

title: Choose linter and type checker; start docs/DEPENDENCIES.md
description: Pick one linter and one type checker as dev-only tools. Verify provenance live (maintainer, repo, advisories, licence, dependency count) and present to Luke for approval before adding. Create docs/DEPENDENCIES.md with the standing rules and rows for every dependency adopted so far.
acceptance_criteria: Luke approved the choices; docs/DEPENDENCIES.md exists with dated rows; both tools run clean on the skeleton.
notes: Provenance checked live 2026-11-16 by subagent; AWAITING LUKE'S APPROVAL, nothing installed. Recommendations: (A) test runner: REJECT pytest 9.2.0 (4 direct deps; CVE-2025-71176 tmpdir handling public 2026-01-22, fixed 9.0.3 on 2026-04-07) in favour of stdlib unittest; subagent says unittest would do for a CLI tool. (B) build backend: ADOPT uv_build (>=0.13,<0.14; zero deps, bundled inside uv, Astral) over hatchling 1.33.0 (5 deps, effectively single maintainer Ofek Lev) and setuptools. (C) linter/formatter: ADOPT ruff 0.17.5 (Astral, zero deps, Rust binary, no advisories). (D) type checker: ADOPT mypy 2.4.1 (5 direct deps, no GitHub advisories); ty 0.0.104 rejected as beta with a High advisory GHSA-vxvm-j4xq-q7m4 (code execution analysing a crafted project); pyright rejected (PyPI package is a third-party wrapper that downloads Node); pyrefly 1.4.1 credible runner-up. title: Foundations: package skeleton, gateways, config
description: Everything other work stands on: the goodall package, its single command, the runner and UI gateways, the config model, and dev tooling. Decisions: bd memories DECISION.

title: Align command and constant names with the glossary's 'work block' and 'prompt gate'
description: GLOSSARY.md settles on 'work block' and 'prompt gate' and says to avoid 'session' for a work block, but the CLI subcommand is 'goodall session start|end|status' and the exit-code constant is SESSION_GATE_CLOSED. Decide with Luke whether the command becomes something like 'goodall block ...' or 'goodall work ...', or whether 'session' stays as the command word and the glossary records that; then rename consistently in cli.py, exit_codes.py, tests, AGENTS.md and open issues.
acceptance_criteria: One term per concept across glossary, CLI help, constants and tests.

title: Human test: what compaction does to the transcript file
description: Luke runs it: in a long interactive session, copy the transcript file, run /compact (and separately let auto-compaction trigger if practical), then compare. Does the file get appended to, rewritten or replaced; do earlier entries remain on disk; does SessionStart fire with source 'compact'; does the session id change? Decides whether goodall's incremental copy needs its keep-both-on-shrink rule.
acceptance_criteria: Append/rewrite/replace answer with evidence saved with bd remember; goodall-fs9.6 updated if the sync design must change.

title: Human test: interactive session endings and blocked prompts
description: Luke runs it in an interactive (not headless) Claude Code session with the logging hooks: record the SessionEnd reason for /exit, Ctrl-C, Ctrl-D, closing the terminal window, and /clear; record what a prompt refused by the UserPromptSubmit gate looks like in the terminal UI and whether the typed text is preserved for resubmission.
acceptance_criteria: SessionEnd reason per ending method and a description of the blocked-prompt experience saved with bd remember.

title: Human test: hooks and transcripts on lid close, sleep and power-off
description: An agent cannot do this; Luke runs it. With a logging hook settings file active in a live interactive Claude Code session mid-turn, (1) close the lid, (2) let the Mac sleep, (3) force power-off. After each, check whether SessionEnd fired and with what reason, whether the transcript JSONL is intact and how many entries were lost, and whether the next session start sees leftovers. Logging setup: the hook-spike folder left by spike goodall-fs9.1 (rebuild from bd memories SPIKE if the temp folder is gone).
acceptance_criteria: For each of the three cases: SessionEnd fired yes/no and reason, transcript intact yes/no, entries lost; saved with bd remember.

title: Pre-register the subscription vs API-key rule for Luke's eval
description: Luke's own eval runs mixed billing. Write down in advance which work runs on which mode so the split is not chosen after the fact. This belongs in the eval's record repo, not in goodall; tracked here so it is not lost.

title: Redaction policy and goodall release
description: Define a redaction policy file for an eval and a command that produces a redacted copy of the records for publication to a separate public location, leaving the private working record untouched. Wait until the record and label formats have settled.
acceptance_criteria: A release run on fixture data removes every pattern the policy names and reports what was removed; the source records are byte-identical afterwards.
notes: Spike finding 2026-11-16: Claude Code telemetry carries user.email, account and organisation ids on every record by default; redaction must cover telemetry files, not only transcripts and journals.

title: Publish goodall to PyPI
description: Claim the name, set up the build and release steps, confirm 'uv tool install goodall' gives a working 'goodall' command. Publishing is outward-facing: Luke performs or explicitly approves it.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh account installs from PyPI and 'goodall --help' works.

title: Release: redaction, publication, corroboration
description: What it takes to publish the tool and, later, a dataset. Decisions: bd memories DECISION.

title: goodall teardown wizard
description: Walks a researcher through winding an eval down in a safe order: final off-machine copy of records, revoking tokens and API keys, closing paid accounts, removing hooks and shell changes goodall added. Goodall guides and verifies; the human performs each account action.
acceptance_criteria: Each step is confirmed or explicitly skipped and the outcome is written to the record repo; hooks and marked shell blocks are removed cleanly.

title: Spike: selecting the API key from a work block's workstream
description: Find the cleanest way for a work block's workstream to choose which per-workstream API key Claude Code uses, and how subscription sessions coexist (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY via op run, apiKeyHelper, or a launcher). Raw keys must never be written to disk.
acceptance_criteria: One recommended mechanism saved with bd remember, with the failure modes observed.

title: Write the open-source README
description: What goodall is, who it is for, install, the three places data lives (tool, record repo, log directory), the data-integrity statement and its honest concessions, what is not supported.
acceptance_criteria: A researcher new to the project can explain where their data goes after reading it.

title: Propose file-exporter improvements to the OpenTelemetry Collector
description: Contribution opening found in spike goodall-fs9.2. Draft for Luke to review and file with open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib (file exporter, alpha, one code owner, seeking more): allow append together with rotation; do not truncate an existing file silently on start (default to append or warn); offer flush or fsync per write. First read that repo's contributing rules and search existing issues; confirm truncation and data-loss behaviour by test (the owner-run tests listed in bd memories SPIKE goodall-fs9.2 PART B) so the report rests on observation, not documentation.
acceptance_criteria: Luke has reviewed the draft; filed issue URLs saved with bd remember.

close_reason: Skills configured for Beads: docs/agents/ files, Agent skills block in AGENTS.md, seven ADRs, seeded GLOSSARY.md. Committed on branch claude/pocock-skills-beads (4 commits), not pushed. Not yet exercised by running a tracker-using skill end to end.

title: Pull provider usage reports for API-key sessions
description: Human-run command that fetches per-API-key usage for a date range using an Admin key held as a human-only secret, and stores the report beside the records so API-key sessions can be checked against the provider's ledger.
acceptance_criteria: Report for a test range saved; command refuses to run inside an agent-driven session.

title: goodall logs: browse records locally
description: Read-only local viewer over work blocks and their raw records, showing raw content verbatim and flagging anything unparseable.
acceptance_criteria: Renders without network access and never writes under the raw record directories.
